title: VF-MT302-ReconcilerDaemonCore
clause: Single crowned reconciler daemon: conditional SurrealDB crown-lease leadership with fencing and expiry, conditional per-worktree claim leases, SurrealDB live-query + resync-tick + boot-orphan triggers collapsed into per-worktree watch flags, Semaphore-bounded JoinSet dispatcher with full jitter, CancellationToken graceful shutdown

scope.summary:
GOAL: Build the reconciler daemon skeleton that keeps the microVM workspace fleet converged: exactly one crowned reconciler task per host, level-triggered reconcile passes per worktree, bounded concurrency, and graceful shutdown - the runtime chassis that MT-303 plugs its state machine into. This is a Handshake-managed in-process tokio task set, NOT a new external daemon (house rule), and it copies control-loop heuristics from kube-rs/Oxide without any Kubernetes/Docker/containerd/Nomad dependency.

LEADERSHIP AND CLAIMS (research P14, translated to SurrealDB): the crown is one account-scoped SurrealDB lease record acquired by a conditional transaction. It carries owner_instance_id, fencing_generation, heartbeat_at and expires_at; one instance wins, losers back off and retry, and takeover increments the fence only after expiry. Each per-worktree pass similarly claims through a conditional SurrealDB transaction with a bounded lease/fencing token. Liveness comes from leases; safety remains the generation predicates on desired and binding writes. No session lock, dedicated PostgreSQL connection, or blocking database waiter exists.

TRIGGER COLLAPSE (research P6-P9): three trigger sources - (a) authenticated account-scoped SurrealDB live-query subscriptions from MT-301, (b) a full-fleet resync tick every 60-300s (configurable, default 120s) that enqueues every non-tombstoned fleet row, (c) a boot-time orphan pass that enqueues everything once at daemon start (the ongoing version of boot orphan reconciliation, per P8) - all collapse into ONE per-worktree tokio::sync::watch activation flag (Oxide RPW pattern, P9: multiple signals collapse to one because the reconciler only needs to know IF it was activated). Triggers carry NO payload; every pass fresh-reads desired row + binding row + observed VM state. An unbounded mpsc of trigger events is forbidden (P9 warns of thundering herds and queue stress).

DISPATCHER (research P15, P17): a dispatcher task drains activated worktrees into a tokio JoinSet of per-worktree reconcile tasks, bounded by a global tokio Semaphore with 2-4 permits (default 3) because CH snapshot restores are IO-heavy; each dispatch applies full jitter (random delay in [0, base)) to kill startup stampedes; boot enqueue orders by priority DESC then freshest lease heartbeat (heartbeat_at_utc, model_lane.rs line 6571) first.

SHUTDOWN AND CANCELLATION SAFETY (research P18, P19): tokio_util CancellationToken cancels TRIGGER SOURCES only (listener, ticker, dispatcher intake); in-flight reconcile tasks in the JoinSet are drained to completion - never task::abort() on a body that may be mid-VM-mutation. select! arms may contain ONLY pure waits (watch.changed(), tick, token.cancelled()); once triggered, the reconcile body runs as a spawned task polled to completion, never inside a losable select! arm.

RESOURCE PRIVACY: the daemon runs under a ResourceAccessContext and only ever sees fleet rows within its exact account/Principal scope (resource_scope.rs OwnerAccountId line 53, ResourceScope lines 147-153; scoped-load precedent worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 1164-1207). The crown-lease record id and permission scope include owner_account_id so one account cannot block or observe another.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: new files src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/vm_fleet/reconciler.rs (daemon, triggers, dispatcher, shutdown) and vm_fleet/config.rs (typed knobs); mod.rs registration; tests. The reconcile BODY in this MT is a seam: it fresh-reads state and calls a trait object (FleetReconcileStep) whose real implementation arrives in MT-303; this MT ships a no-op-plan implementation sufficient to prove chassis behavior.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Typed config (vm_fleet/config.rs):
   pub struct FleetReconcilerConfig { pub resync_interval: Duration /* clamp 60..=300s, default 120s */, pub max_concurrent_restores: usize /* clamp 2..=4, default 3 */, pub dispatch_jitter_max: Duration /* default 2s */, pub live_query_reconnect_backoff: Duration /* bounded and jittered */ }
   Constructor validates clamps and rejects zero values with typed errors.
2. Crown:
   pub struct FleetReconcilerCrown { lease: SurrealCrownLease /* fenced, heartbeated, account-scoped */ }
   pub async fn acquire_crown(store: &SurrealFleetStore, scope: &ResourceScope, instance_id: InstanceId) -> Result<FleetReconcilerCrown, FleetReconcilerError>  // conditional SurrealDB lease acquisition or typed Contended result; heartbeat/expiry/takeover increments fencing_generation and stale holders cannot commit.
3. Trigger plumbing (vm_fleet/reconciler.rs):
   struct WorktreeActivation { flag: tokio::sync::watch::Sender<u64> }  // monotonically bumped activation counter; receivers collapse bursts
   async fn listen_task(surreal, access_context, activations, token)  // authenticated official-SDK live-query streams over the scoped desired/binding/lease records; parses ONLY the worktree key hint to select which flag to bump; on parse failure or unknown worktree, bumps ALL flags (fail toward resync, never toward silence); on connection loss, reconnects with backoff and then bumps ALL flags because notifications during the gap are lost (P7)
   async fn tick_task(config, store, activations, token)  // every resync_interval: list_desired() and bump every flag; label the pass trigger source TICK
   boot pass: same as tick_task once at startup before the listener is trusted, label BOOT
4. Dispatcher:
   async fn dispatch_task(pool, store, semaphore, joinset, activations, token)  // for each activated worktree: acquire semaphore permit, apply full jitter sleep, open a transaction, conditionally acquire the per-worktree SurrealDB claim lease and fencing token; if claimed by another, drop silently (the other claimant reconciles); else spawn the reconcile body into the JoinSet with the permit moved into the task
   Reconcile body seam: pub trait FleetReconcileStep: Send + Sync { async fn reconcile(&self, ctx: FleetReconcileCtx) -> Result<FleetReconcileOutcome, FleetReconcilerError>; }  // ctx carries fresh-read desired record, binding record (via WorktreeVmRegistry::durable_binding, worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 969-977), trigger-source label, and the claim transaction; MT-302 ships NoopReconcileStep that records the pass and releases the claim
5. Shutdown:
   pub struct FleetReconcilerHandle { token: CancellationToken, join: JoinHandle<()> }
   pub async fn shutdown(self) -> Result<(), FleetReconcilerError>  // cancel token -> listener/ticker/dispatcher intake stop -> JoinSet drained with join_next() until empty -> crown lease released LAST so a successor cannot be crowned while our in-flight passes still run
6. Trigger-source labeling: every pass records its trigger source (BOOT | TICK | live-query change event) in the pass record handed to the step seam, so MT-306 can label FR events tick-vs-notify (P8: drift caught by tick must be visible).
7. HOUSE RULES: all Rust; SurrealDB only, no SQLite; no K8s/Docker/containerd/Nomad crates; no new external daemons - the reconciler is a Handshake-managed in-process task set; disk-agnostic paths; no names with spaces; per-owner CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ../Handshake_Artifacts/ in every proof command.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read MT-301's landed store module, worktree_vm_registry.rs lines 935-1000 (resolve/durable_binding read paths), and the official SurrealDB Rust SDK live-query API in the locked SDK version.
2. Implement config.rs with clamped typed knobs.
3. Implement conditional SurrealDB crown-lease acquisition, heartbeat, expiry/takeover and fencing; release or expire the lease only after in-flight work drains.
4. Implement watch-flag activation registry keyed by worktree_id, with bump-all fallback semantics.
5. Implement listener, ticker, and boot pass; label trigger sources.
6. Implement dispatcher with conditional SurrealDB claim leases, semaphore bound, full jitter, JoinSet spawn; define FleetReconcileStep + NoopReconcileStep.
7. Implement shutdown ordering (token -> drain JoinSet -> release crown).
8. Tests against real SurrealDB (Spec-Realism Gate): two daemon instances produce one live crown holder; expiry/takeover increments the fence and invalidates the stale holder; crown key is account-scoped (two accounts crown concurrently); live-query change event bump wakes exactly the target worktree flag; listener reconnect bumps all flags; tick enqueues all rows; conditional SurrealDB claim-lease contention dispatches each worktree at most once per pass; semaphore never exceeds max_concurrent_restores (assert with a concurrency counter in a test step impl); shutdown drains an in-flight slow step to completion and never aborts it.
9. Run proof targets; record measured output. Implementer never marks COMPLETED.
forbidden_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/sandbox/** (no adapter changes; MT-303 consumes the adapter through the registry)
acceptance_criteria: AC-302-1: Exactly one reconciler per account scope holds a live SurrealDB crown lease with monotonically increasing fencing generation and bounded expiry; a live two-instance test proves one winner, expiry/takeover fences the stale holder, and two accounts never contend.

AC-302-2: Per-worktree dispatch claims use conditional SurrealDB claim-lease transactions with fencing; a live contention test proves a worktree is dispatched at most once concurrently and stale claim holders cannot commit.

AC-302-3: SurrealDB live query, resync tick (60-300s clamp, default 120s), and boot orphan pass all collapse into per-worktree tokio watch activation flags; no mpsc trigger queue exists in the module (grep proof), and triggers carry no actionable payload.
AC-302-4: Listener connection loss triggers reconnect-with-backoff followed by a bump-ALL-flags resync, proven by a test that kills the listener connection.

AC-302-5: The dispatcher JoinSet is bounded by a global Semaphore clamped to 2..=4 permits with full-jitter dispatch delays; a live test with an instrumented step proves observed concurrency never exceeds the bound.

AC-302-6: select! arms in the module contain only pure waits (watch/tick/cancellation); reconcile bodies run as spawned JoinSet tasks polled to completion; code review + grep proof confirm no side-effectful future inside a select! arm and no task::abort on reconcile tasks.

AC-302-7: Shutdown cancels trigger sources, drains in-flight reconciles to completion, releases the SurrealDB crown lease last, and refuses further fenced writes; a live slow-step test proves the step completes during shutdown.
AC-302-8: Every pass carries a trigger-source label (BOOT | TICK | live-query change event) into the FleetReconcileStep seam.
AC-302-9: The reconcile body is a trait seam (FleetReconcileStep) with a shipped NoopReconcileStep; MT-303 can plug in without chassis edits.
AC-302-10: No new external daemon, no SQLite, no K8s/Docker/containerd/Nomad dependency; grep proof over the module and Cargo.toml.

implementation_notes: IMPLEMENTATION GATE: gated on WP-1 IV verdicts + merge to main (expansion_provenance.implementation_gate); MT-301 must land first.

The crown lease is liveness; generation and fencing predicates are safety. Never treat a live lease as permission to skip generation-checked writes, and reject a holder whose fencing generation is stale.
Full jitter means uniform random in [0, max), not fixed stagger (research P15/P17).
The 60-300s resync clamp is deliberate (research P8): shorter intervals mask event-path bugs; trigger-source labels exist so drift-caught-by-tick is visible in MT-306.
SurrealDB live-query reconnect MUST be followed by an account-scoped bump-all resync because events during a disconnected interval are not authority; canonical records are re-read.

Reconcile bodies must be crash-equivalent to a kill: MT-303 journals intent before side effects, so draining is a courtesy, not a correctness requirement - but never abort mid-VM-mutation (research P18/P19).
Implementer never marks COMPLETED; verdicts belong to the WP validator.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Daemon chassis MT; the operator-facing fleet panel and FR event emission are MT-306. Pass records with trigger-source labels are the projection seam.

target_entries: Workspace fleet > Reconciler daemon (crown model, trigger sources, resync interval, concurrency bound)
Workspace fleet > Shutdown behavior (drain semantics, why in-flight VM operations complete)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Pass records carry trigger-source labels; FR emission is MT-306. Record DEFERRED-to-MT-306 with the pass-record seam as evidence.
Crown acquisition failure, listener reconnect, and dispatch errors should emit diagnostic events via the open diagnostic-event API if present; otherwise DEFERRED-with-reason.

The reconciler is a long-lived in-process task set whose death matters: register the daemon with Palmistry when available; otherwise DEFERRED-with-reason, with crown-lease heartbeat expiry and fencing as the minimum crash signal.

risk_if_missed: No convergence engine exists: desired state (MT-301) is written but never enacted, crashed VMs stay dead, orphans persist beyond boot, and any ad-hoc replacement would rediscover the thundering-herd, dual-writer, and lost-notification failure modes the research basis explicitly catalogs.

risks: RISK-1: Two reconciler instances both believe they are crowned (pool-recycled connection, lock taken on a pooled conn that gets returned), and both mutate the same VM fleet.
RISK-2: A missed live-query change event or transport disconnect silently strands a worktree in a wrong state until an operator notices.
RISK-3: Startup stampede - boot enqueues every workspace and unbounded parallel CH restores exhaust host memory/IO.
RISK-4: Shutdown aborts a reconcile task mid-VM-mutation, leaking a half-created VM or a paused-never-resumed workspace.
RISK-5: The reconcile body is embedded in a select! arm and silently dropped when another arm wins, leaving side effects half-applied.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Crown lock lives on a dedicated non-pooled connection held for daemon lifetime; generation fencing rejects stale writers regardless; AC-302-1 two-instance live test.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): Resync tick re-enqueues everything on a 60-300s clamp and listener reconnect bumps all flags; AC-302-3/AC-302-4 tests.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): Global Semaphore clamp 2..=4 + full jitter + priority/heartbeat ordering; AC-302-5 instrumented test.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Shutdown drains the JoinSet before crown release and never calls abort(); AC-302-6/AC-302-7 grep + drain test.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): select! arms restricted to pure waits with bodies spawned to completion; AC-302-6 code review + grep proof.
